claim: Premise: the JS divergence 'suffers from vanishing gradients when distributions do not overlap, a common phenomenon when datasets come from different sequencing technologies, leading to failed training'; a discriminator 'can perfectly separate the batches, leading to gradient saturation and training instability'.
original_evidence: Literature only (cites WGAN, key 10.5555/3305381.3305404). No experiment measured batch support overlap or showed a failing discriminator.
basis: Checked WGAN (arXiv 1701.07875) Thm 1 and Example 1 (JS = log 2 for disjoint parallel lines) and Arjovsky & Bottou 2017 (arXiv 1701.04862) Thm 2.4 (vanishing generator gradients for the minimax cost as D approaches D*); the same paper states the -log D step 'doesn't necessarily suffer from vanishing gradients' but is unstable. So the theory covers the saturating / near-optimal-discriminator case, not automatically the bounded fool loss the plan now uses (verified in scvi-tools 1.4.2 AdversarialTrainingPlan.loss_adversarial_classifier(predict_true_class=False) and 5709a98 _fool_loss). 'Leading to failed training' is contradicted by the paper's own data: the 1-step discriminator integrated (higher ASW-batch in 6/6 Table 2 cells, higher ARI in 5/6). 'Common phenomenon' was never measured; the revision's E6 overlap numbers were computed on the double-normalised prep (audit C2) and must be recomputed. RIGOROUS TEST: (a) model-free support overlap per dataset and batch pair on the corrected prep; (b) log discriminator accuracy and generator-side ||grad_z L_adv|| per batch during training for disc-1, disc-10 and each critic. CONFIRM if on low-overlap datasets discriminator accuracy -> 1 while its generator gradient norm collapses and batch metrics stall, whereas critic gradients persist; REFUTE if discriminator gradients stay comparable to the critics' and it reaches comparable batch scores. Arjovsky & Bottou 2017 is not in reference.bib and should be cited.

claim: Novelty: 'no study has rigorously isolated the adversarial objective' / an isolation 'has not been performed'.
basis: One web search (this audit) returned only this work's own public versions: bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.11.12.688061 (v1 titled 'Wasserstein Critics Outperform Discriminators in Adversarial Deconfounding of Gene Expression Data'; v3 = the submitted abstract) and the project's GitHub README. No systematic literature search was done here, so absence of prior work is not established. RIGOROUS: structured search over adversarial / OT / MMD batch-correction methods (AD-AE, ResPAN, IMAAE verified below; MMD-ResNet is already in reference.bib but uncited; scDREAMER, an adversarial-classifier VAE, appeared in a search-result reference list); soften to 'to our knowledge' and cite the earlier preprint versions.

claim: Method contribution: 'We introduce a multi-class reference-based Wasserstein critic' (multi-headed, per-head GP on source-reference interpolates, stratified minibatches guaranteeing reference samples).
basis: Read cd64f05: the head and W1-dual loss exist as described, but (i) the binary and reference-sensitivity runs used the GP fallback D4 (interpolation toward random cells of the whole minibatch, every head incl. the reference head penalised), so the described GP was used only in the multibatch runs; (ii) the generator back-propagates the full W estimate including the reference term (z not detached), contradicting l.217-221. 5709a98 keeps the reference critic with the reference index passed explicitly (correct GP) and adds pooled and barycenter targets (src/wcd_vae/wcd/critic.py). RIGOROUS: state the implemented generator objective exactly and present the reference critic as one of three critic formulations.

claim: 'The Wasserstein critic yields superior mixing' / 'is a stronger integrator' / 'achieved higher iLISI scores across all scenarios'.
where_in_manuscript: Abstract (l.105); Introduction (l.134); Results 1 'Integration Performance' (l.319); Results 3 (l.401); Discussion (l.422, l.424)
original_evidence: Table 2 iLISI critic vs discriminator, 6/6 cells: Pancreas 0.736/0.620 (p=0.0064) and 0.740/0.648 (p=0.0987); Immune 0.713/0.603 (4.8e-4) and 0.689/0.562 (0.0040); Lung 0.622/0.498 (0.0175) and 0.455/0.370 (0.0080); Fig 2; Fig 4 iLISI above the discriminator at every nominal lambda in {0.01..0.5}.
basis: Produced by the submission pipeline with D1 (NB fit to log-normalised values), D2 (train/test PCA misalignment inside the LISI kNN graph), D3 (sampled z), D4 (GP fallback in the binary runs), D5 (critic 10 updates vs discriminator 1), D6 (unbounded discriminator loss), on the scCRAFT backbone, iLISI-centric. Re-testing Table 2's 36 reported p-values with Holm leaves 6/36 significant and only Immune-balanced among the iLISI rows. Only valid evidence now: atac_small counts pilot (PROVISIONAL: 1 dataset, 3 seeds, 239 ep / batch 512 / n_latent 30, i.e. before the stock-default switch; discriminator still 1-step with the unbounded max-CE loss; reference = alphabetical index 0; scIB overall min-max scaled within the pilot's own run set). There, at lambda=1 (conditioned) the reference critic has iLISI 0.681 vs discriminator 0.556 (batch score 0.808 vs 0.669), but the discriminator reaches iLISI 0.782 at lambda=20 and overall scores tie (0.646 vs 0.640). RIGOROUS: per dataset x decoder, batch-score vs bio-score Pareto fronts from the fixed lambda grid (5 seeds) for reference/pooled/barycenter critics vs disc-1 and disc-10 (bounded loss). CONFIRM if the critic front gives a higher batch score at matched bio score (seed CIs separated; paired test across the 8 datasets); REFUTE if fronts overlap or the discriminator front dominates. Matched-nominal-lambda comparisons are not admissible (CE and W-estimate scales differ).

claim: Local/global discrepancy: ASW-batch 'did not show the same effect'; 'the discriminator effectively aligns global distributions, the critic better resolves fine-grained batch structures within local cell neighborhoods'.
original_evidence: Table 2 ASW-batch higher for the discriminator in 6/6 cells (Pancreas 0.894/0.930, 0.895/0.932; Immune 0.853/0.872, 0.873/0.878; Lung 0.870/0.910, 0.861/0.898) while iLISI favoured the critic.
basis: Same defects; D2 specifically corrupts the kNN-based (local) metrics, whereas ASW was computed on test cells alone. R1.major.1 asks for this to be a central result. Provisional counterexample from the atac_small counts pilot (PROVISIONAL: 1 dataset, 3 seeds, 239 ep / batch 512 / n_latent 30, i.e. before the stock-default switch; discriminator still 1-step with the unbounded max-CE loss; reference = alphabetical index 0; scIB overall min-max scaled within the pilot's own run set): at lambda=1 the reference critic leads on BOTH iLISI (0.681 vs 0.556) and ASW-batch (0.972 vs 0.957). RIGOROUS: per-metric lambda curves for iLISI, kBET, graph connectivity (local) vs ASW-batch, PCR comparison (global); per-dataset Spearman between local and global batch metrics across configs; test whether the critic-minus-discriminator sign differs between scales at matched lambda and at matched batch score. CONFIRM if the sign flips between local and global metrics on most datasets; REFUTE if the orderings agree.

claim: The critic over-corrects: 'reduction in cell-type purity', 'prone to over-correction resulting in collapsed cellular representations'; consistent integration-conservation trade-off.
where_in_manuscript: Abstract (l.105); Introduction (l.134); Results 1 'Biological Conservation' and 'Summary' (l.321, l.325); Discussion (l.424, l.432)
original_evidence: Table 2: cLISI worse for the critic 6/6, ASW-cell lower 6/6, ARI lower on Pancreas and Immune (0.670/0.942, 0.692/0.938, 0.447/0.556, 0.439/0.554); Fig 4 critic cLISI rising with lambda.
basis: Pipeline defects D1-D6, AND the backbone contained a triplet loss added explicitly 'To mitigate latent over-correction' (l.172) plus a cosine term at weight 20, so the conservation axis was largely set by auxiliary losses that the stock-scVI plan removes. The abstract attributes over-correction to the 'reference sensitivity analysis', which (Fig 5) only measured iLISI/cLISI spread over references. A later native-backbone wave (also on the C2-bugged prep) reversed the direction; neither is valid now. atac_small counts pilot (PROVISIONAL: 1 dataset, 3 seeds, 239 ep / batch 512 / n_latent 30, i.e. before the stock-default switch; discriminator still 1-step with the unbounded max-CE loss; reference = alphabetical index 0; scIB overall min-max scaled within the pilot's own run set): critics' bio score collapses at lambda>=5 (reference 0.220, pooled 0.227) while the discriminator keeps 0.551 at lambda=5 but collapses at lambda=20 (0.296): every arm over-corrects, critics at lower nominal lambda. RIGOROUS: compare bio metrics (cLISI, ARI/NMI, isolated-label F1/ASW) and direct readouts (per-type purity, rare-type recall, label-transfer F1, sim1/sim2 ground truth) at MATCHED batch score, relative to the lambda=0 control. CONFIRM if at equal batch score the critic's bio is lower on most datasets (CI-separated); REFUTE if equal or higher.

claim: PAGA: 'a trend of cell type collapse'; Discussion: the manifold 'was more warped in the case of the Wasserstein critic, forcing unrelated cell types together'.
original_evidence: PAGA Spearman lower for the critic in 6/6 cells but p<0.05 only in Lung-balanced (1.2e-4; survives Holm); the other five p=0.057-0.44.
basis: Custom metric (cd64f05 hyperparameter.py compute_mean_paga_spearman: PAGA on the ~20% held-out test cells vs each technology's raw-PCA PAGA) computed on D1-D3 embeddings; the Discussion upgrades a 1/6-significant trend to a mechanism. Not part of scIB-native scoring (trajectory conservation is disabled: no pseudotime annotations). RIGOROUS: replace with cell-type confusion matrices / per-type neighbourhood purity on all cells with seeds (R2.6). CONFIRM 'forcing unrelated types together' only if confusion between distinct types rises for critics at matched batch score.

claim: Sensitivity to confounding structure: 'no systematic pattern across datasets' (discriminator iLISI dropped on Immune but 'actually improved in the Pancreas dataset'; critic dropped on Immune and Lung).
basis: The scenario manipulation did not do what it claims. Computed from Supplementary Table S2: the 'balanced' binary sets keep strong batch-cell-type dependence (Cramer's V 0.33 pancreas, 0.42 lung, 0.33 immune vs 0.33/0.54/0.45 unbalanced), and pancreas balanced differs from unbalanced by just the 2 inDrop3 t_cells (3,605 -> 3,603 cells), so the Pancreas 'improvement' (0.620 -> 0.648) compares near-identical data and is run-to-run variation. RIGOROUS: define 'balanced' as composition-matched (subsample every batch to identical cell-type proportions) vs natural composition, 5 seeds, test the scenario x method interaction. CONFIRM a confounding effect only if unbalanced degrades batch or bio metrics beyond seed noise.

claim: 'The discriminator acts as a conservative regularizer'; the '"weak" integration characteristic of discriminators acts as a protective measure against over-correction'.
basis: Confounded by D5/D6: the critic took 10 adversary updates per encoder step and the discriminator 1 (cd64f05 hyperparameter.py:195), with an unbounded generator loss; nominal lambda is not comparable across objectives. Weaker integration conserving more is the trade-off curve itself, not protection. RIGOROUS: include the budget-matched disc-10 arm and compare at matched batch score. CONFIRM 'protective' only if, at equal batch score, the discriminator conserves more biology; REFUTE if the advantage disappears when integration is matched.

claim: 'Integration difficulty increases with the number of batches'; 'a decrease in performance across all scenarios for both methods'.
original_evidence: Fig 3 (iLISI and cLISI vs number of batches; pancreas 2->9, immune 2->4; balanced and unbalanced).
basis: Multibatch runs used the correct reference GP but D1-D3, D5, D6 apply. Part of the decay is a metric ceiling: scaled iLISI cannot exceed about (1/sum p_b^2 - 1)/(V-1) under perfect mixing; from Table S2 sizes this drops 0.965 -> 0.703 when immune's 1,022-cell smart-seq2 batch is added (3 -> 4 batches) and 0.933 -> 0.807 for pancreas (3 -> 9), comparable to the discriminator's immune decline in Fig 3. The balanced sets also change composition with V: balanced immune goes from 10 shared types (29,282 cells) at V=3 to 4 myeloid/DC types (8,928 cells) at V=4, and balanced pancreas drops to alpha/beta/delta/gamma once SMARTer enters (V>=6). RIGOROUS: ceiling-normalised iLISI (or batch-size-balanced subsamples), full scIB suite, composition held fixed across V.

claim: The critic 'scales poorly with the number of batches'; 'The Discriminator Out-scales the Wasserstein Critic'; the critic 'degrades significantly faster'.
original_evidence: Fig 3 iLISI crossovers (critic higher at V=2, lower from V~3-4); iLISI only; no statistical test.
basis: Reviewer R1.minor.1 objected to iLISI-only evidence. Defects as above; 'significantly faster' was never tested; ceiling and composition confounds (previous item). The revision's E8 numbers came from an invalidated pipeline. RIGOROUS: batch-count series (batches added in descending size, as originally) on >=3 datasets with >=4 count batches, 5 seeds, full scIB suite, all formulations incl. pooled/barycenter and disc-10, at the pre-registered lambda (or per-V Pareto fronts). CONFIRM if the critic-minus-discriminator difference in ceiling-normalised batch score and in bio score declines with V (interaction slope CI excludes 0) on most datasets; REFUTE if flat.

claim: Mechanism: a single-reference 'topological bottleneck' / 'uncoordinated radial projection topology creates a geometric bottleneck', whereas the discriminator's joint V-way objective 'implicitly coordinates the latent geometry'.
original_evidence: None beyond the iLISI trend; no reference-free critic was run.
basis: Flagged by R1.minor.1, R2.3 and R2.5. Now directly testable with the pooled and barycenter critics (no privileged batch; 5709a98 critic.py). CONFIRM a reference-design effect if the reference critic's scaling deficit vanishes for pooled/barycenter and tracks reference coverage; attribute it to the W objective only if every critic formulation degrades while the discriminator does not. Until tested, write 'single-reference design' without geometric language.

claim: Because the scaling drop 'occurs equally in both biologically balanced and unbalanced scenarios, it cannot be attributed to the reference batch lacking specific cell types'; hence 'a fundamental architectural limitation'.
basis: The exclusion logic holds for the balanced sets (all batches share the same cell types by construction: cd64f05 data.py balance = intersection), but the evidence comes from the defective pipeline, the balanced composition itself changes with V (see 'Performance Decay'), and 'architectural limitation' requires the pooled/barycenter control.

claim: Critic performance 'is dependent on a topologically dense reference batch'; iLISI outliers 'are strictly driven by the cell-type representation present in the target reference batch'.
where_in_manuscript: Abstract (l.105); Results 4 'Sensitivity to Batch Completeness' (l.411); Discussion (l.428)
original_evidence: Fig 5 box plots over every reference choice (iLISI roughly 0.36-0.44 pancreas balanced, 0.32-0.40 unbalanced, 0.33-0.40 immune); no per-reference coverage analysis.
basis: Contradicted by the paper's own design: in the balanced scenario every candidate reference contains the same cell-type set, yet the pancreas balanced spread is as large as the unbalanced one (read from Fig 5), so cell-type representation cannot be the 'strict' driver; no coverage covariate was analysed. These runs also used the GP fallback D4 and alphabetical reference indices. RIGOROUS (new experiment, original section 4): reference sweep, every batch as reference, >=3 seeds each, at the pre-registered lambda on pancreas (up to 8 batches once CEL-seq inversion / Fluidigm rounding are added and SMARTer is excluded), immune (4), sim1 (6), atac_large (11 via batchname_all); regress batch/bio scores on reference coverage (fraction of dataset cell types present), Shannon entropy and size; seed variance as the noise floor; composition-matched negative control. CONFIRM if coverage explains variance beyond size and seed noise; REFUTE otherwise. The plan's entropy rule fixes a single reference and does not test this.

claim: 'Because the Wasserstein objective enforces a strict optimal transport plan', query-specific populations are projected onto unrelated reference populations, 'effectively erasing true biological variance'.
basis: W1 between normalised batch distributions does require matching all mass, but the critic estimates W1 through its dual and no transport plan is computed, and no per-cell-type evidence was shown (R2.3: 'which cell types collapse'). RIGOROUS: with a reference lacking type T (natural, or T held out of the reference), measure where query cells of type T land (label-transfer predictions / confusion into reference types) for the reference critic vs pooled/barycenter and the discriminator. CONFIRM if type-T cells are absorbed into reference types specifically for the reference critic.

claim: 'Both the Wasserstein critic and the discriminator exhibit broad optimal operating windows on the iLISI metric, with the critic performing consistently higher'.
original_evidence: Fig 4 = inner-CV validation records (40-epoch models), lambda in {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5}.
basis: D1-D3, D5-D7; the grid spans 1.7 decades and the discriminator's lung iLISI is still rising at lambda=0.5 (optimum not bracketed); nominal lambda is not comparable across objectives. Because the submission's NB term was averaged over 2,000 genes, its lambda grid corresponds to about 20-1000 in summed-NB (scVI) units, so it cannot be ported. Pilot critics peaked at the lambda=1 grid floor (bracketing failed again). RIGOROUS: fixed log grid bracketing each arm's optimum and collapse (planned 0.01-30; check the upper end reaches discriminator collapse on every dataset), lambda curves with 5-seed bands, plus curves against achieved batch score. CONFIRM 'broad window' if the score stays within the seed CI of its maximum over >=1 decade of lambda.

claim: 'For the cLISI metric, the discriminator maintains a broad, flat curve that is highly insensitive to the choice of adversarial coefficient'; the critic's cLISI rises with lambda.
basis: Same defects and grid limits. Provisional counterexample from the atac_small counts pilot (PROVISIONAL: 1 dataset, 3 seeds, 239 ep / batch 512 / n_latent 30, i.e. before the stock-default switch; discriminator still 1-step with the unbounded max-CE loss; reference = alphabetical index 0; scIB overall min-max scaled within the pilot's own run set): the conditioned discriminator's bio score falls with lambda (0.621, 0.551, 0.296 at lambda 1, 5, 20; isolated-label F1 0.826 -> 0.490). RIGOROUS: per-metric bio lambda curves with seed bands; claim insensitivity only if bio stays within the seed CI across the bracketed grid.

claim: Wasserstein models need 'approximately ~24% more training time per epoch'; the discriminator 'achieves faster convergence'.
where_in_manuscript: Methods (l.240); Supplementary Note 1 (Fig S1 caption, Table S1)
original_evidence: Table S1: critic minus discriminator wall-clock +19.6% to +27.5%.
basis: Holds only for the large scCRAFT backbone, where 10 critic steps on detached 256-d z were cheap relative to the 1024/512-unit VAE. On the plan's stock scVI (128 hidden units) the measured cost (project context: atac_small, batch 128, RTX 3080, single lane) is ~7 s/epoch reference critic and ~9 s pooled vs ~1 s discriminator (~2 s at 10 steps), i.e. 3.5-7x. Convergence was never measured (fixed epoch budgets). RIGOROUS: report per-epoch and per-fit wall-clock for every arm on one GPU, including disc-10.

claim: 'In scenarios with strong confounding or disjoint distributions, the discriminator frequently failed to mix local neighborhoods effectively. In contrast, the Wasserstein critic forced mixing even when batches were initially far apart.'
basis: Pipeline defects; initial separation was never quantified; scaled iLISI of 0.37-0.65 is not a failure to mix, and lung's perfect-mixing ceiling is about 0.53 (Table 1 sizes 22,771 vs 6,485), so the discriminator's 0.370 is ~70% of attainable. RIGOROUS: relate per-dataset gains to measured pre-integration support overlap (R1.major.2). CONFIRM if the critic's batch-score advantage (at matched bio) grows as overlap decreases.

claim: Practical recommendation: the Wasserstein objective 'is ideal for scenarios with severe, disjoint batch effects and overlapping cell types, whereas the discriminator scales more effectively in fragmented atlases with disjoint cell types or sensitive cellular boundaries'.
original_evidence: None: no experiment varied batch-effect severity against cell-type overlap.
basis: RIGOROUS: stratify datasets by measured support overlap and cell-type overlap (immune_hum_mou cross-species as the disjoint control; sim1/sim2 controllable) and test the objective x regime interaction on the lambda curves. Keep the recommendation only if that interaction is significant.

claim: A Wasserstein barycenter (learned 'virtual' center, 'the geometric median of all batch distributions') would combine the critic's gradients with the discriminator's global robustness.
where_in_manuscript: Discussion 'From Reference Matching to Wasserstein Barycenters' (l.428)
basis: Now in the plan (5709a98 barycenter = W1 critic against 64 learnable anchors moved by the generator optimiser). Cautions: audit M2 found barycenter configs shrink the latent (max|z|<1 in 78-100% of configs at lambda>=50), so the zstd pilot must precede conclusions; and 'geometric median' mis-describes the cited Agueh-Carlier object (abstract: a barycenter generalising McCann's interpolation, i.e. a mean). CONFIRM if the barycenter matches the reference critic's batch score with discriminator-level bio and no reference or scaling sensitivity.

claim: 'The primary limitation of the Wasserstein objective in its isolated form is its propensity for biological over-correction'; future work should use adaptive / annealed adversarial weights.
basis: Depends on the over-correction and protection claims. An annealing schedule already ships in stock scvi-tools: AdversarialTrainingPlan uses kappa = 1 - kl_weight when scale_adversarial_loss='auto' (verified, 1.4.2 source); testing it as one arm answers R2.2's 'scheduling strategy' with the tool people actually use.

claim: The Wasserstein distance 'remains a continuous and differentiable metric even when distributions are non-overlapping, providing robust gradients that drive alignment regardless of the initial separation'.
basis: WGAN Thm 1 (verified): W is continuous everywhere and differentiable almost everywhere if the generator is locally Lipschitz and a regularity assumption holds; false for JS/KL. A gradient-penalty critic only approximates the 1-Lipschitz potential (soft constraint, WGAN-GP), so 'robust gradients regardless of separation' describes the ideal distance, not the estimator. Reword accordingly.

claim: Prior Wasserstein methods (ResPAN, IMAAE) add auxiliary steps that obscure the adversary's contribution; IMAAE attributes reference-alignment failure to a 'lack of constraints' with sparse anchors, 'motivating their decision to enforce a global Gaussian prior'.
basis: Verified: ResPAN abstract (WGAN + random-walk mutual-nearest-neighbour pairing + fully skip-connected autoencoders); AD-AE abstract (autoencoder + adversary predicting the confounder). IMAAE full text (PMC10056671): 'lack of constraints' occurs for an autoencoder experiment in which batches with fewer cell types are anchors (their Fig 11a); IMAAE keeps an anchor batch as decoder target and adversarially matches q(z) to N(0,I) with a WGAN-GP-form loss (the word 'Wasserstein' does not appear). It also reports a GAN that works on two batches but under-corrects with three or more, which is prior evidence relevant to the scaling question. The 'motivating their decision' link is the authors' interpretation; rephrase.

claim: The unbalanced scenario is 'known to drive severe over-correction and the ablation of biological signal in standard adversarial deconfounding'.
basis: Needs a citation or a test via the composition-matched vs natural design (see 'Sensitivity to confounding structure').
